utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. All the accused are present. Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer. The Defence teams are all here, but I notice the absence of Mr. Bourgon and Mr. Haynes and Mr. Ostojic. Okay. Good afternoon to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. We are going to continue with your testimony and hopefully finish. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. I would like to take you back to the topic of the police forces staff on Mount Jahorina. What do you remember? Was the commander of that staff the same throughout the staff's existence, or did various people take turn in that place?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were very often very common changes in that place. I believe that Dusko Jevic was the first, then Borovcanin, then Goran Saric, but I am not sure about the last two.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Mr. Borovcanin as being the commander of that staff for a while. To the best of your recollection, when was that approximately?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I believe that it was in April 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And after him, can you remember who took over from him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Goran Saric.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we please look at the following document, which is 4D66.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We can see that this is a dispatch by Commander Goran Saric, the commander of the special brigade, dated 13 June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please zoom in to see when Mr. Saric was appointed.

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 13th of you June.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now that we have looked at this document, I would like to ask you one more thing about Mr. Saric. You see that Goran Saric will be in command of the police staff on Jahorina and that his deputy will be the assistant commander Mladenko Borovcanin. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, what was Mladenko Borovcanin's position in the special police brigade at the time? What was his function?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any case, he was the assistant commander of the brigade, but I am not sure what he was in charge of. I believe that he was in charge of some sort of training.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one correction for the transcript. It's on page 2, line 44. There is something here. It's on page 2, line 22. I was referring to Mr. Borovcanin Mladenko, so just to have a clear record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: With regard to this document, now that we have had an occasion to see the document and the date on it, does this correspond with the time when Mr. Saric took over the command of the staff?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you've told us that Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin was the staff commander before him, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And before that, we also saw documents dating from -- to April 1995 where Mr. Jevic is mentioned as the staff commander?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now, I would like us to sidetrack a little and ask you something about the special brigade. In addition to taking part in combat, do you remember that the special police brigade performed other duties in crisis situations? Are you familiar with any other type of jobs that the brigade was involved in?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special police brigade tasks did not concern waging a war, but they concerned their own territory, policing in the territory. During the war they were trained to perform such tasks that had to do with the maintenance of public law and order, prevention of large scale disruptions of public law and order, providing security for mass or large-scale gatherings, providing security for various individuals and facilities, prevention of the infiltration of sabotage and terrorists groups, and also assisting the population in cases of disasters, natural or others.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would like us to look at a few documents that might shed some light on what you have just spoken about. May the Court please produce 4D631.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This document has not been translated. The document is short, however. It's a dispatch by the Ministry of the Interior dated 23 September, 1994. Somewhere in the middle of the document, it says: "I hereby command members of the diving team of the special brigade police," under 1, "Ljubisa Borovcanin," under 2, "Mladenko Borovcanin," and there are other names, a total of eight of them. And just for the record, let's look at the last part of the document of the dispatch, which says: "They insisted an enormous effort in searching the lake in Zvornik for three days and managing to find the bodies" -- or rather, "the body of a person mentioned herein." My question to you is this, sir. Now that we see this document, does this document illustrate some activities that members of the special police brigade were engaged in?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I participated in this event. I was also involved in the execution of this task and was commanded for that. Under number 2, Mladenko Borovcanin, and under number 3, Goran Markovic are specials from the -- the special police unit that was active before the war. Even Tomislav Tutovic, they were all -- Tomislav Krstovic, they were all trained before the war to perform diving tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We will no longer need these -- this document, and just one more question about the staffs. Do you know whether the police forces staffs were also formed for some other situations, not only for the command and control of the police units? Were there some other examples for which the police forces staffs were ever established?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was dictated by practice. As soon as a situation occurred on the ground which called for the participation of several segments of the police force, in such situations a staff would be established composed of the representatives of such formations for an easier command and control of these units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the following document. You are going to see it on the screen before you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the Court please produce 4D632. And again, unfortunately, I don't think we have received the translation of this document. I believe this is the last document for which a translation is still pending. The rest have been translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We can see that this is a dispatch by the Ministry of the Interior sent on the 17 February 1996. Let's look at the following page, please. Let's look at the last two paragraphs on the second page. This is an order which says: "I hereby order to launch the Winter '96 Operation and establish a security staff that will be composed of" - under 1 - "Ljubisa Borovcanin, the chief of admission, the head of staff." And in order to provide a complete picture of the situation, could we please scroll up to the top of the document. You see that the national assembly of Republika Srpska was in session under special circumstances. Was that the reason for the establishment of the staff?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was post-Dayton Accords. This was post-war, and both sides were unhappy. The specificity of the situation consisted in the fact that the Serbian people did not accept what our representatives had signed, so the assembly session had to be secured.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But war was still going on in the Republika Srpska, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And on the entire territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this had nothing to do with the -- the enemy's side. These were our own inner struggles. There were a lot of people present, and this called for a larger-scale security, and several police units had to participate in that from the security centres, from the brigades. A staff had to be established because somebody had to be in control.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And we can see on this side that Mr. Borovcanin was appointed as the head of this staff, and if we move to the following page we will see who else was on the staff, who were the other members of the staff. I don't think it says -- it is necessary, but we can see the functions of the members of the staff. It says the chief of the administration of public security, the chief of the public security station in Pale, and I don't think we have to go any further. And if you look at the following paragraph, you will see that it says the security staff will draft a plan with concrete measures of operative, physical, technical, traffic, and other forms of security and will appoint persons in charge. The document was signed by Minister Dragan Kijac. Now that we have seen this document, can you please tell me whether this would be a situation in which the police forces staff was established for some activities which were not can combat activities by their nature?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right. This was not about any combat activities. This was about providing security in order to prevent any disruptions or incidents. This was common practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now, I would like us to move on to the events that took place in 1995. Tell me just briefly. My questions are going to be very relative, and if there is no need I am going to ask for clarification and further explanation. But first of all, tell me, do you know that at one point in time in 1995 a -- a staff was established in Pale, a staff took control and command of police forces?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I often go there to deliver mail or to receive tasks. The staff was billeted in a catering facility called Tron.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When was that? When was that staff established to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure, but in 1995 it was operational.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And can you please remember the reasons for which the staff was established?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the reasons were because of the enemy offensive that already commenced in spring 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to have a look at the following document, 4D139.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for it to appear on the screen, let me tell you that it's a document from the office of the Minister of the Interior of Republika Srpska. It's dated the 16th of June, 1995. It contains conclusions from the meeting of the Minister of the Interior, a meeting that was held on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have a look at the second page of the document. Let's have a look at item A1. AD1, it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As we can see, it says after having discussed the current military situation in the republic as a result of an intensive enemy action against all lines in Republika Srpska, the following conclusions were adopted. Item 4 says: "In the Tron facility in Pale, form a staff for commanding police units." [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Hold it because we are not --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises. The microphone was not switched on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed. Thank you. You need to repeat please, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Having examined the document, and you already told us that you are aware of the existence of this staff, and you also said that it was located in the Tron facility in Pale, we could see that it's the 16th of July, 1995, that that is the date. So does this help you to find your bearings with regard to when this staff was actually established?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was a staff -- headquarters of the staff, but the staff was previously formed. I know that the commander was Mr. Tomo Kovac, Tomislav Kovac. The chief of the cabinet is the signature. This is from relevant officers from the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska. I know almost all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And obviously on the 16th of June, well, that's the date when this decision was taken, the decision to form the staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move on to another subject now. Let's have a look at 4D272.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is a law on modifications and amendments to the law, on applying the law on army and conditions of an imminent threat of war or of a state of war. The date is the 12th of May, 1995. It was published in Official Gazette 7/95. And I'd like to have a look at a very brief law. Let's first have a look at item 2 -- paragraph 2 under Article 1. It says that "Recruits enlisted for the VES, for the military police. May be signed to do their military service in special units of the Ministry of the Interior." The following paragraph in this article says that: "The contingent of recruits from the previous paragraph shall be trained according to the training programme for members of special units of the Ministry of the Interior." So I would first like to ask you whether at the time you found out that this law had been amended, this law that allowed recruits to serve in units of the Ministry of the Interior, and when I say to serve there, I mean to do their military service there.

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have this law in front of me, but I'm familiar with these provisions in the form of dispatches received in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I'd now like to have a look at the following document, 4D626.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were familiar with the amendments to the law, and you also said that you'd been informed about these amendments in dispatches. Have a look at this document. Now, is this what you were referring to? This is, in fact, a dispatch?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's a -- the kind of dispatch I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And as we can see, it's addressed to various parts of the MUP --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is kindly asked to repeat what he said, as there was overlapping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There was overlapping, and the interpreter would like you to repeat what you said, please, in your last answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. At the end -- well, the dispatch is addressed to various departments but to everyone in the end. So the entire Ministry of the Interior was familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. My following question with regard to the law that we have examined and the dispatch that we have seen, in accordance with these amendments to the law, at some point in time did a group of recruits start arriving on Jahorina for the sake of training as stated in this law?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of this law we started preparations for doing one's military service within the Ministry of the Interior; and at the time, during this period of time, were commenced on Jahorina. And in order to see how this would function, because we weren't sure about this, we had a pilot project that was to include 35 recruits on Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, as far as you can remember, when did this, roughly speaking, happen?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this was in mid-June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So training of recruits who were doing their military service was concerned?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were young men whose duty it was to do their military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I'd now like to deal with another category that arrived on Jahorina at one point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a look at 4DP1. It's an order from the president of the Republika Srpska, Radovan Karadzic, dated the 16th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the strictest measures for combat preparation are being introduced for combat-readiness. Let's have a look at the first page, item 3. Item 3, paragraph 2, it's in the lower part of the document. Here it says that the Ministry of the Interior and of -- the Interior will do the necessary for the return of military conscripts from the Serbia and to allocate them to the units of the armed forces. I'd now like to have a look at page 3 in this document in the B/C/S version, the second paragraph where it says: "The army Main Staff shall use the command to secure the reception of mobilized recruits. They will accept them and introduce them to the units," and they will also provide them with the necessary training. Having seen this document, tell me, do you remember any activities that have to do with bringing in military conscripts, and this was done by the Republika Srpska MUP?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with this order in the form of internal dispatches in the Ministry of the Interior, and I know that this was in fact done.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to make a distinction in the training centre on Jahorina, as you have already said, we had individuals who attended a policemen's course; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Then we had recruits who were doing their military service in MUP units?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And this, now, is the third category that is trained in the centre for training individuals on Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the time it wasn't in the form of a centre. At the time we called it a camp, a training camp. But the number of men increased as a result of these men being brought in from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now that we are discussing this category, we are talking about military conscripts who left the territory of Republika Srpska to avoid serving in the armed forces. What was the name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The usual name, deserters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, at some point in time, did these deserters start arriving in the centre?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within a two-day period, from the beginning of the second half of June, I can't exactly remember the date, but in two days over 200 such individuals arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to have a look at the following document, 4D511. It's a report on the work of the special police brigade for June 1995, and if we could have a look at the second page. Very well. Could we zoom in a bit? I am interested in the third paragraph on the second page. It's page 1 in the English version. It's somewhere in the middle of the paragraph, and it says the camp for receiving and training military conscripts have been returned from the SRJ, has started operating -- or started operating on Jahorina on the 22nd of June, 1995. It was organised by the senior command officers and the brigade instructor team.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, now, having seen this document, does this period of time correspond to the time-period that you remember as being the time when the centre for training on Jahorina commenced with its work?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this only confirms what I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have a look at 4D119 now. It's a dispatch from the deputy minister of the MUP dated the 23rd of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We have it on the screen now. And in this dispatch, the deputy minister is informing the president of Republika Srpska about the number of military conscripts delivered by the Serbian MUP. You can see that in the first paragraph of the dispatch. So, tell me, here it says that a total of 1.586 conscripts were handed over to the VRS forces, the Republika Srpska army, and out of that number 149 conscripts were handed over to the MUP staff on Jahorina. Does this, roughly speaking, confirm what you have been saying about the arrival of these people who were sent to Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. But this number, 149 conscripts, was augmented. Another 70 or 80 individuals should be added to that number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. When bringing these individuals in, as far as you can remember, were there any mistakes made? Were any individuals brought in who were soon sent back to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were several dozen individuals who had mistakenly been brought in because perhaps they didn't have ID on them at the time. But as soon as evidence was found, they were sent back immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's now have a look at 4D628. It's a dispatch from the staff taking in military conscripts from SRJ -- from the SRJ. Its headquarters are in Bijeljina. It's addressed to the deputy minister of the MUP on the 27th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If we look at the first paragraph, the introduction, can we see from it that a request arrived from the Serbian MUP for certain conscripts to be urgently returned to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and a list of eight names is referred to?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were people like that in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now let's look at the following document, 4D629. This is an order by the president of the Republika Srpska sent to the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska and the MUP of the Republika Srpska on the 28th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We see in this order that people who had been delivered to Republika Srpska by mistake are ordered to return -- or to be returned, rather. My question in this regard is as follows: This document and the previous one that we just saw, do they refer to what you were just talking about; i.e., that there was a number of people who had been delivered to Republika Srpska by mistake?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the same, but these are interventions that reach the office of the president of the Republic, and hence, his order. Basically, it's about the same cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now let's look at another document in this regard, 4D630 is the number. Again, its a dispatch by the deputy of the Ministry of the Interior, dated 13 July 1995, sent to the president of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And we can see in this dispatch that the deputy minister informs the president about the implementation of the MUP Serbia action to return military conscripts to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and that a total of 43 persons who had been mistaken by a mistake to the republic, mostly citizens of the state of Serbia, were returned. My question about the three documents, do they demonstrate the principle based on which the return of these individuals was carried out?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is correspondence between the Ministry of the Interior and the president of the republic about the same thing, about dealing with the same problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I understood the procedure well, the MUP Serbia sent their request, then the president issued his order for some individuals to be returned. This was done by the MUP Republika Srpska and informed the president of Republika Srpska of that.

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What about the individuals who were not returned to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia who had been brought to the centre in Jahorina for training? According to the best of your recollection, were they treated differently then the other categories of trainees, and if your answer is "yes," could you please explain the difference?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a difference in attitude. It was a very peculiar group of young men, aged between 25 and 35, a very non-homogenous group. First, they had to be kept together, keep them confined, so to speak, so that they could not run away. And then we had to work with them, and we had to turn them into a -- into soldiers. That's what we called them at the time. That's what we called the process at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But my question applied to the other two categories, recruits serving in the army and trainees for the policemen. Was the treatment different?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first two category were volunteers, and the third category had been forced to be there. They were not really confined. They were not enclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just for a clarification. When you say they were volunteers, that means that they were there on their own will? I just want to avoid any confusion.

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Police trainees and military conscripts were there of their own will, and the others had been forced to be there. Able-bodied men who had fled to the federal state of Yugoslavia had been forced to be there to perform their civic duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now that we're talking about the state category that we will call deserters, had they had their personal IDs removed from them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many of them did not have them at all. But those who did, yes, the documents were taken from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And when it comes to the freedom of movement, were they restricted, the deserters? Did they have any restrictions on their freedom of movement?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jahorina Mountain, where we worked, they were not restricted in movement. There was nowhere to go. They could go to the nearest newsstand to buy newspapers. They adapted to that, but they were not allowed to leave the mountain, although they asked for that very often. For example, they wanted to go to see the doctor. They would be taken there but under escort. We wanted to prevent any situations of desertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether they were organised in one unit or several units? How was their stay organised?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were organised in two companies of three or four platoons. After such a long time, I can't remember exactly. I know that they were organised in two companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at another document, which is 4D352. This is a daily report from the training camp on Mount Jahorina. The assistant of the special police brigade sends that to the Ministry of the Interior, and the date is the 31st of July, 1995. Can we scroll down a little?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Who signed this document, please?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am the signatory. Actually, I signed the document on behalf of my commander, Dusko Jevic. I drafted the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In this report, we can see that there are 251 [as interpreted] police trainees and 31 recruits on the list.

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And they are on Mount Jahorina for training, and we can see in the lower part that one person left the camp without permission. His name is mentioned in here. I would like us to focus on the handwritten part of this document in the top part of the page. Could you please read the handwritten part. What does it say here?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Pekic informed the administration of the crime police about this so that they will be able to issue a search warrant and inform the Serbian MUP thereof." This is a daily report. It was our obligation to send daily reports on all the changes that took place in our camp. This was a change and a wanted notice had to be issued, and the handwritten remarks were probably added in the minister's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's now look at the following document. 4D353 is the number of the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: [Realtime transcript read in error, "Madam Fauveau"] Mr. Lazarevic, just before you leave the document, I don't know how significant it is, but in the transcript at page 18, line 8 and 9, it talks about the document recording 251 police trainees and 31 recruits, whereas the document itself refers to 201 conscripts and 35 recruits. So I think the transcript is probably in error. I don't know if it was translation or what it was, just for clarity of the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. You are absolutely correct, and it does say 201 military conscripts. [Interpretation] 4D353 is the document I would kindly ask the Court to produce. Again, this is another daily report from the training camp on Jahorina. The assistant commander of the special police brigade sent this document to the Ministry of the Interior, and the date is the 1st of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Does this document also bear your signature?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And again, we can see a handwritten remark: Pekic told Bijeljina UKP, crime police administration, about this deserter to issue a wanted notice and inform the MUP, the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia. Does this tell you something about who had the authority to issue wanted notice and bring the deserter in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If I could add something to what my colleague, Judge Prost, said. Line 25 of page 18 describes the words of Judge Prost as being those of Madam Fauveau. That's not correct, so the transcript will be corrected in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now that we have seen the two documents -- I apologise. I can see now that you have not answered my question about the authority over issuing wanted notices. Does this document illustrate that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, neither the training camp nor the command of the special police brigade were authorised to issue wanted notices.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now that we have seen the two documents, do they show that there were both recruits and military conscripts in the camp, and do these documents also show what kind of training they underwent?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number of 35 recruits had already started their training according to plan, and this was just the continuation of the implementation of this plan. And as for the 200 military conscripts, i.e. deserters, we only did the most basic infantry training starting with the lining up, moving, greetings, and then we took it day by day. Our situation gradually improved.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now tell me whether the deserters received any theoretical education.

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was nothing by way of theory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You've already told us about the deserters' training, and you said that their training differed from the other categories. Was it better, more intense, less intense?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was much simpler, and it had to be forced upon them, if I may put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How long did their training last? Was it shorter than the training of the other categories of individuals? I am referring to the two categories that we referred to; i.e., police trainees and recruits who were serving their -- in the units of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their training was really short, maybe not even a month, and then they would be sent off into battle. Our comment was that they started resembling soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now that you have said that, in your view were the deserters really capable of participating in combat activities? Did you enable them to do that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since they had all served in the army before, they had all undergone compulsory military service, they did not differ much from any other members of the army of Republika Srpska. This particular preparation was not enough if it had been the only thing, but it could do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever learn that one of the units composed of deserters was supposed to be sent off to Srebrenica or was to be engaged in the events surrounding Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this was on the 11th of July, 1995, when the first unit -- actually, the first company from the camp was lined up and sent on a mission. At that time, I was really busy. I was over the head, and my memory is jogged by the subsequent dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you find out where that company went?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only found that they were heading in the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you personally present when the unit was preparing to leave or when it left?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On a number of occasions, yes, but briefly while passing by.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, was the departure of the unit a departure that had been previously planned, or was the unit suddenly engaged and sent off?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All this happened all of a sudden. We in the camp were also surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, how many individuals were there in that unit?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have the first company that we mentioned in mind, perhaps about a hundred men.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, were all these men in the company deserters?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, apart from the company commander and the instructor from the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, as far as you can remember, what sort of weapons were they issued with when they left?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had automatic and semi-automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, apart from these weapons what sort of equipment were they given, if they were given any particular kind of equipment?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they had a minor quantity of flak jackets - I don't know what make, perhaps Borovo ones - and they had camouflage uniforms; the colours were simple colours, and that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were they given heavier weapons, perhaps grenades or something like that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We didn't have any grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me who the commander of the unit was, the commander of that company that left on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 11th of July, 1995, Mendeljevic [Realtime transcript read in error, "Mendarovic"] Djuric led the 1st company. It's not Mendarovic. It's Mendeljevic, LJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. This will be corrected. This often happens when we have names. What I wanted to ask you is whether you saw Ljubomir Borovcanin at any point in time when this unit of deserters was setting off?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how this unit was transported to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think buses were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that that unit, that company, was to be part of a joint-MUP forces and Mr. Borovcanin had been designated as the commander of those forces?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And let me ask you the following: Do you know that another company was sent to the wider area of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a day or two after the 1st company.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This was also a company of deserters from Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, do you know who issued the order? Did an order arrive, an order that you saw with regard to sending this 2nd company there? Did you hear anything about this if you didn't personally receive such an order?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, but such an order could only have come from the police forces staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you say the "police forces staff," are you referring to the staff in Tron that we have already spoken about?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were matters that they were responsible for.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And tell me now, do you know where these companies, the 1st or the 2nd company, stayed while they were in that area?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know because I wasn't familiar with that area, in any case, with the area of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know that while they were there in the field they carried out certain activities, and if they did, what kind of activities?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain that I know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And one more question about the matter. Do you know who was in command of these companies, or rather, were they subordinated to anyone, and if so, to whom?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was quite natural that the chief of the camp commanded these companies. As to whom they were subordinated to in the field, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, as far as you can remember, can you remember how long these units stayed in that area around Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was between for six and eight days.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, now, did the members of the unit, did the deserters having stayed in that area around Srebrenica return to the centre, to the training centre, on Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, most of them returned to Jahorina, although some were wounded and some were perhaps even killed in the action. But some, since they were near Drina, near the river Drina, had the opportunity of deserting again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, now, did some of the deserters or some of the members of the special police brigade ever tell you anything about the tasks that they had during that period while they were in the field?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't tell me anything about that. If anything was said, it was to the effect that they had to secure roads and do things like that. I'm not certain whether these are memories I have that date back to that period or whether they are subsequent memories due to the media, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know anything about the events that took place in July 1995? Do you have either personal knowledge, or did you receive information about such events? Do you have any knowledge about events in a place called Sandici?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any direct information, only information that ordinary people had, information that ordinary people had through television, the newspaper, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any direct or indirect knowledge? Did you hear anything from deserters or members of the special police brigade with regard to events on the 13th of July, 1995, in the agricultural cooperative in Kravica on the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that. All I know about Kravica is what I learned from the news, when there were reports on Serbs who had been killed at the beginning of 1993, at the time of Orthodox Christmas 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think part of your answer to the previous question hasn't been recorded in the transcript. Did you say that you didn't even know where Sandici was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know where Sandici is located, and I still don't know where Sandici is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, when returning from the field, what was the status of these deserters? Did they continue to receive training? Were they provided with any additional training?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we still trained them for a while. Most of them agreed to bear the arms and wear the uniforms of the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, after this event, were these people asked to join the army or the MUP of the Republika Srpska? Did they join these bodies or both of them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we believed that the men were valuable and if they accepted the offer to remain in police units, well, in that case, they remained in the police units, whereas the others were sent to military units, or rather, they were handed over to the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just a few more questions before we move on to another subject. Can you tell me whether the Jahorina centre also provided training in the second half of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We've been discussing the period during which it was a training camp, and after this situation with the deserters, I can't remember exactly, but I think that it was in August or September over 200 men arrived to do their military service. I don't know the exact number of recruits concerned. They were young conscripts, and they came to do their military service, and from that time onwards, the name of the centre was a centre for training, and we had a new structure for command and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's have a look at the following document, 4D95. It's a report for the special police brigade for the period January to September 1995; although, here it says it's up to the 15th of October, 1995. What I would like to have a look at is page 5 of the B/C/S version of the document, and it's page 4 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you see that under number -- under Roman (iv) it says "training." In the second paragraph, it says, In the period from the 19th of June, 1995, until the 2nd of August, 1995, training was provided for 205 deserters who had been brought into the camp for taking in and training deserters. They had been brought in from SR Yugoslavia. It says, Currently on the training camp on Jahorina, there are 184 recruits who are doing their military service in the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska. Tell me, does this correspond to what you can remember about that period and to what you can remember about the number of recruits who were doing their military service in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a report for a nine-month period. It's been compiled on the basis of the monthly reports for the year, although at the time we didn't have any deserters, but this is mentioned on the basis of previous reports and dates provided. But at the time, we were working with recruits, and this the correct number of recruits that we were working with. We are talking about the regular army here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And before we have the break, I'd like to have a look at one more document, 4D94. It's a report on the work of the Republika Srpska MUP in 1995. Let's have a look at page 6 in the document, in the B/C/S version. It's page 2 in the English version. Can we please zoom in just a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, what I would like to hear from you is this: I would like to draw your attention to paragraphs 4, 5, and 6 in this document. In paragraph 4, it says that in March 1995 a training course for policemen was organised for 195 trainees. Then in the following paragraph, it says that the instructor team also trained 202 military conscripts on Jahorina and the course lasted two months and that in June, 235 military conscripts who are serving in the MUP units are being trained on Jahorina in a centre that had just been established. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is just a compilation of monthly reports, which just repeats the things that we have already discussed here dealing with the training course for policemen, i.e., people whom police units sent for additional training. The instruction team also trained military conscripts on Jahorina, and the course lasted for two months. Those were military conscripts that were brought in from the federal republic of Yugoslavia, i.e., deserters, and this indeed was the time when the training centre on Jahorina had been established based on the camp for reception, and there we at that moment had 235 a recruits or -- who are serving their military service in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And we can see all the three categories that underwent training in the training camp on Jahorina, and we can also see the time intervals when their training was organised.

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now just one more question about this topic. According to your recollection, how long for did the centre continue to operate?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was until maybe February or March, perhaps, when we received an order to bring our operations to an end on Mount Jahorina, to vacate the facilities of the Jahorina Hotel that would be prepared for the accommodation of refugees from the municipalities of Ilijas, Vogosca, and Ilidza, I believe. There was a time when Serbs were leaving en mass, they were leaving Sarajevo en mass.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just for the clarity of the record, I would like to ask you something. What year are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1996, the beginning of 1996, and I believe that it was in the month of March, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I am going to go on to the another topic, so maybe it's a convenient time to the adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic, we will have a 25-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic. How much longer?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I believe 30 more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would like us to move on to a completely different subject, which is informing within the special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's first look at document 4D509.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is a report on the engagement in combat of the special police brigade in the Majevica theater of war in 1995 -- in April 1995. Very well. Could we please first look at the cover page that is in front of us, and now we will have the English version as well. I've already described the nature of the document. Have you had an occasion to see this and documents of this type?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a very customary way of reporting, was carried out in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at the last page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Off mic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise Mr. Borovcanin's handwriting in this report as the person who submitted the report?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin's initial.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In terms of the form of this report, would this be a typical report on the engagement of the special police brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very typical.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What is the nature of this report? Is that an external report or an internal report within the special police brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is internal reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now, based on the information entered in such an internal report, what happens to the information next?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is reporting to the immediate superior. I suppose that this followed some sort of verbal reporting, and this report subsequently serves as part of a future compilation report, which is sent out monthly or quarterly or annually, and it is filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at the following document, which is P92. Let's look at the last page of this report, please. The bottom part, if this could be zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the signature on this report?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is this Mr. Borovcanin's signature?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that this is not his handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's move on to 4D510. This is another report on the engagement of the forces of the special police brigade and other forces in the Srebrenica '95 operation. As far as the wording of the document is concerned and its contents, these are practically identical with the previous document but this copy also has a cover page unlike the other ones. Can we please look at the last page of the document. Very well. Can we now move to the last segment of the document. Can we scroll down a little, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the initial on the document, and can you tell us who the initial belongs to? The document has been initialed --

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This seems to be the same report, but this is now Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin's initial.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think it would be appropriate for the witness to take off his earphones at this point because I would like to the address the Trial Chamber and maybe have some stipulation with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see if he understands English first. Do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A few words, maybe. Yes and no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's too little, but not a few. All right. Remove your headphones, please. You are addressing the Trial Chamber in English, I suppose --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yes, that's what I'm going to do. Your Honours, the position of Mr. Borovcanin Defence, and I believe the Prosecution shares the same position, is that this is the original of the document. Last time, when Mr. Borovcanin was on his custodial release, he managed to find two of these reports, the first one that we saw from the Majevica theater of war, and this is the other one. As soon as we found those documents, we gave two originals to the Prosecution in order to just make all additional checkings, whether they have any objections to this, and I was informed by Mr. Thayer that they can confirm that these are original documents. Those are 4D509 and 4D510.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you confirm that, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Then we can proceed now. All right. It's okay. This is harmless. So let's proceed straightaway. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can I go back to the first page of 4D510, please. This document seems to have been drafted on the 5th of September, 1995, and it concerns a period in July 1995. Can you explain, why was the report drafted in September 1995? What might be the reason?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that the person who drafted the report did not find the time to do it sooner. However, for the purposes of collective reporting and statistical reasons, he subsequently drafted it upon the insistence of his superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We saw a report from Majevica as well. Would you say that this would be the same type of reporting as the previous one? The report that we have in front of us, would that be the same kind of report as the one from Majevica that we saw previously?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the same kind of reporting that fall under the obligation to file reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now look at the following document, which is 4D511. This is a report on the work of the special police brigade for June 1995. The document contains three pages; it's a three-page long document. Can we please take a look at all the three pages before we start commenting upon the document. And now, can we please dwell upon the third page of the document a bit longer. And can we please scroll down, just a little bit. In the bottom left part of the document, we see the initials SM/VZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who the initials belonged to?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are my initials, Milan, and there was the typist, Veljko Zeljko. I often had to draft these reports, these monthly reports. They were compiled on the basis of reports from all units of the brigade and police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just note that I think we are in open session, and I don't know whether we need to do something about that. I don't want to say anything further.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think -- I think it's safe enough. We can proceed. But thank you very much, Mr. Thayer, for pointing that out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, the report we have just seen, is it a typical monthly report from the special police brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were particular reports that were also drafted for each month.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's just go back to the first page very briefly. We can see a number in the top left-hand corner; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And monthly reports had such protocol numbers, monthly reports from the special brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Each one was -- if we remember the previous ones, the report on action in the Srebrenica battlefield in Majevica, they didn't have such numbers. Is that because they were internal documents or documents that are sent -- monthly reports that are sent, reports from the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Internal reports that we had a look at form part of this report, but only in so far as they are a collection of reports, a summary of reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's have a look at one more document, 4D95. It's a report on the work of the special police brigade for the period January to September 1995, and it says that the report concerns a period from the 1st of January, 1995, until the 15th of October, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is this an external report from the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a report addressed to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And here, we can also see that there is a protocol number on this document; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, you've already seen this document. I won't go into its contents, but is it a typical periodical report from the special police brigade? If you like, have a look at it. Refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a periodic report on the brigade's work. We're dealing with nine months.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I just have a few more questions. In the Republika Srpska MUP, were there a number of individuals or just one individual whose surname was Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area around Sarajevo, this is a well known surname. In the police force itself, I know five or six Borovcanins, some of whom are my friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But to be a little more concrete, in the special police brigade were there a number of individuals who had the surname "Borovcanin"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin, Mladenko Borovcanin, the deputy command of the brigade; and Danko Borovcanin, a member of one of the brigade detachments; and Borovcanin in the Sarajevo centre of public security had this surname; and there were some others, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, was Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin usually addressed as Ljubisa?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, there were very few who were aware of the fact that his name was Ljubomir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that in the MUP there was one other individual whose name was Ljubisa Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know someone called Ljubisa Borovcanin. He was a -- he was in the police in Sokolac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a look at the e-court system, document P3393. It's a dispatch dated the 10th of March, 1997. It concerned a proposal for the ranks of authorised officials in the forensic -- in the crime police in Sarajevo, in the CJB. If we have a look at the last paragraph in the document, a suggestion is made that Ljubisa Borovcanin be granted the rank of major, a chief of the section for economy crime prevention. Is that the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, an inspector for economic crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that the Borovcanin from Sokolac, the one I mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the man I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is that the same man as this person here in the courtroom, or are these individuals different individuals?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are different individuals, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: A few more questions for the end. Tell me, when did the Borovcanin Defence team contact you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the summer of this year. That was the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you then have other contact, and for how long, if so?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very briefly. In September, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Apart from these two occasions and excluding the time that we have spent on preparation together here in The Hague, did you have any other contact with the Borovcanin Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And just a few more questions before I conclude. Your testimony shows that you obviously know Mr. Borovcanin. Since when have you known him?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have known him when -- in the winter of 1993, 1994, he was designated as the deputy brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what is your opinion of Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he is a man who is exceptionally talented, well educated, dignified, a man without vices.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I notice Mr. Borovcanin would like to communicate with you or he doesn't agree with the witness or is there ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: With Your Honour's permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to communicate with your lawyer? Yeah, he does.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Sir, I must apologise for this slip of the tongue. I mentioned his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether you know whether Mr. Borovcanin in the course of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina was wounded at some point in time? If so, what do you remember about the event?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on the battlefield with him when he was seriously wounded. I went to visit him in hospital in Banja Luka. He was very seriously wounded, and so I was surprised that three or four months later he had managed to recover and return to carry out his task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me when this happened, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in December -- no, November, towards the end of November or between October and November. The first time I visited him in the hospital in Banja Luka was on the 21st of November, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to have a look at all the documents. Unfortunately, I haven't had the time to put them into the e-court system. The first one is a letter of release dated the 9th of November, 1994. Could we have it on the ELMO, please? It's a letter of discharge from the hospital. [In English] I apologise, also, to my colleagues from the Prosecution and the Trial Chamber. I was not sure whether I would use these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Feel free to have a look at it, have a look at the entire document, which is by your side. I think it's quite clear. We can see that Mr. Borovcanin was wounded as a result of an explosion - that's what it says here - "and his stomach was wounded and his lower limbs. This was the result of firearms (mine)." Do you remember this? Do you remember these events in the wounding of Mr. Borovcanin? Is this what you were mentioning?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I've been talking about. I was in the field. I remember that period. I remember that event, and this letter confirms the fact that he was taken to the closest hospital, and then he was transferred to another hospital in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And finally one more document I would like to have a look at. Could we place it on the ELMO. We seem to have a minor technical problem with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suggest in order not to lose time that we have a look at it, and Mr. Thayer has a look at it, and then any of your colleagues who wish to have a look at it, very quickly, and then give it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am illiterate in the language, so I'll just accept my friend's representation of what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Does anyone wish to have a look at it from the Defence teams? Okay. We can proceed. Eva, give it to the witness, please, and we will proceed. You're going to tender this document in any case, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you've now had the opportunity of having a look at this document. It's a confirmation dated the 8th of August, 2000, from the ministry of veterans of the war in Republika Srpska. Can you tell us what level of disability was established for Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Luckily, I don't have such a confirmation, but Mr. Borovcanin, according to this document, is a war invalid of the sixth level or category.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And we have a percentage here?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 60 per cent of permanent disability, is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No questions for the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau. Thank you, Madam Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: One question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Witness, I just want to ask you this. You described yesterday how in late July 1992 after leaving Jahorina you joined a unit that was operating at a checkpoint in the direction of Sekovici, and you went on to say that that unit had been tasked with neutralizing the Yellow Wasps. Who was the leader of that unit, the unit that you joined?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The members of my unit that I mentioned, and I said that towards the end of July and perhaps on the 1st of August, 1992, I said I met them at the checkpoint of the Zvornik-to-Sekovici road. Well, at that time, this unit was led by our first command of the special unit, Mr. Milenko Karisik.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Josse. Mr. Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: No questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon to you and to Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My name is Nelson Thayer. I will be asking you just a couple of questions on behalf of the Prosecution this afternoon. You testified yesterday that a police forces staff was set up in February or March of 1995 at Jahorina. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you told us that the reason for setting up that police forces command staff there was to obtain operative information but also to prepare for an expected spring offensive by the Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not correct in that we didn't have to obtain any information. We already had the information on the basis of which such a staff was established. But given that way events unfolded, we could see that everything had been correctly predicted and that the information was, in fact, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, that anticipated spring offensive, in fact, occurred, did it not, as an attempt to break the siege of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the motives of the enemy side, but it is true that the offensive gradually became more intense throughout that year, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you told us today about a new police forces staff that was established in Pale sometime later, perhaps in May or June of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. And this was just an innovation and raising the level and paying more attention to certain things because the person who was appointed the commander of the staff was the assistant minister or the deputy minister, whatever Mr. Kovac was at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you were shown a number of documents yesterday that were signed by Dusko Jevic as the commander of the staff of the police forces Jahorina-Trnovo. Those documents were dated April of 1995. Do you recall those documents, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So just the one thing that I wanted to clarify from what you said today was, was that police forces staff co-existing with the staff in Pale once the Pale police forces staff was established?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just said that the situation gained a more serious dimension. The staff on Jahorina ceased to exist, and its tasks and duties were taken over by the staff that was housed in the Tron facility, in that catering facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In the Tron facility?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you remain in Jahorina, or did you transfer to Pale or travel between the two? Can you just share that with us?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was obvious from my previous testimony. The staff was given a camp for training, and then this became the training centre. So we never moved from Pale. Our dealings with the staff in Tron were of a purely technical nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So I just wanted to clarify. You remained at the training camp in Jahorina and travelled to Pale from time to time when you had something administrative or technical that brought you there; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When we needed assistance, when we needed logistics support, and when we needed to submit our reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you no doubt were aware of the military activities that were underway during this period of time on the Sarajevo front given your proximity to it and the fact, perhaps, that you actually lived there for some time. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right. I was not an eyewitness of all these events, but I was aware of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And as I think you've alluded to, the offensive intensified as did the Serb forces' response to it and activities with respect to it; in other words, the fighting became fierce in June and early July. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: MILAN STOJCINOVIC [Resumed]
